A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same ProLIP research. Their main text, Appendices A–D, equations, figures, and tables support reliable comparison despite layout changes.

before.justification: v2 reports original zero-shot classification, retrieval, prompt re-weighting, ablation, and robustness results in Sections 4 and Appendix C.

after.justification: v3 retains these original empirical results and adds a qualitative observation from preliminary long-text fine-tuning in Appendix C.8.

M1.justification: Appendix C.8 adds a briefly described LongProLIP adaptation, fine-tuning ProLIP on long text and extending context from 64 to 256 tokens. The core ProLIP architecture, losses, and Bayesian Prompt Re-Weighting procedure remain unchanged.

E1.justification: v3 adds training with long-context text for the LongProLIP extension, although the datasets are unnamed. The 13 benchmarks newly listed in Appendix B.3 already have results in v2's Table C.1 and therefore do not represent added benchmark coverage.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged across the main comparisons, ablations, architecture comparisons, and filtering experiments. LongCLIP is newly cited as a fine-tuning precedent, without a reported comparison against it.

E3.justification: The added LongProLIP study introduces long-text-only fine-tuning and a 256-token configuration. Existing experiments retain their reported settings, budgets, metrics, and testing procedures; detailed protocols for the extension are not supplied.

E4.justification: Appendix C.8 adds a brief qualitative assessment of general zero-shot performance after long-text-only fine-tuning. Existing loss ablations, hyperparameter sweeps, hierarchy analyses, and occlusion/PGD tests are retained unchanged.

E5.justification: Repeated-run, seed, confidence-interval, and statistical-testing information is unchanged. The newly described 'significant performance drop' is qualitative and comes without a statistical test.

E6.justification: Existing numerical results in Tables 1–3 and C.1–C.9 are unchanged. Appendix C.8 newly reports that fine-tuning solely on long text can substantially reduce general zero-shot performance, but provides no scores or quantified comparison.

T1.justification: The mathematical definitions, loss derivations, Bayesian prompt-weighting formulation, and covariance/mixture reasoning in Sections 3 and Appendices A and D are unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same central contributions and performance claims, including 74.6% ImageNet accuracy and 75.8% with few-shot prompt re-weighting. LongProLIP is presented as an auxiliary extension.

C2.justification: v3 explicitly identifies the existing 64-token context boundary as an applicability limitation and warns that long-text-only fine-tuning can harm general zero-shot capability. Earlier interpretations and the diagonal-covariance limitations remain unchanged.

D1.justification: The Reproducibility Statement now enumerates available ProLIP checkpoints and specifies LongProLIP ViT-B/16 weights fine-tuned with different datasets. v2 provided only the general checkpoint collection link; existing implementation details and access URLs are retained.

R1.justification: v3 adds primary references for existing benchmarks, including CLEVR, EuroSAT, and Dollar Street, plus LongCLIP and the LongProLIP technical report. The central positioning relative to deterministic and probabilistic vision-language models remains unchanged.

P1.justification: The section sequence and most prose are retained. Changes include typo corrections, publication-status text, expanded benchmark and checkpoint descriptions, and the short long-context paragraph.

P2.justification: The same figures and tables are retained, with conference headers and appendix layout changes. Several displays move, including Table C.6 from page 23 to page 25, without substantive changes to their contents.

improvement.justification: v3 modestly improves documentation through better benchmark attribution and explicit checkpoint descriptions, while Appendix C.8 clarifies a practical context-length limitation and fine-tuning tradeoff. The core numerical evidence and theory remain unchanged, and the long-context extension is unquantified and sparsely documented, so the overall gain is limited.
